Turns the always-on service notification into a clock showing 12:45:08 with the date — works on every phone.

Flips the hidden Android “clock seconds” switch, which SystemUI watches live. Fully automatic via Shizuku (no computer) — or one pasted ADB command if you prefer. Heavily-skinned clocks (OneUI / ColorOS) may ignore this key — if the top-left clock doesn\'t change, use the notification-panel seconds clock above instead.

Seconds Clock can flip the hidden status-bar “seconds” switch for you — pick a path:

• Automatic (Shizuku): no computer. One-time Shizuku install + on-screen pairing; the app does everything else.

• Manual: copy the ADB command and run it from a PC.

Shizuku is a free, open-source helper that lets trusted apps make system changes with a tap — no computer needed.

1) Install it from Play
2) Open Shizuku and follow its Start instructions (Wireless debugging pairing shows a code on your own phone)
3) Come back here and tap the seconds button again — everything else is automatic.
Shizuku is installed but not running yet
Open Shizuku and tap Start (it pairs through Wireless debugging; it stays active until reboot). Then come back and tap the seconds button — Seconds Clock takes it from there.
Done. If the status-bar clock now ticks seconds your ROM supports it — otherwise it ignores the key and the notification-panel clock is your seconds clock.
Notification clock running — swipe down to see 12:45:08
Or long-press the home screen → Widgets → Seconds Clock
OnePlus/ColorOS: Batteries → Seconds Clock → Allow Auto-launch & Don\'t optimize.\nSamsung/OneUI: Device care → Battery → Background usage limits → add Seconds Clock to Never sleeping apps.
Your launcher can\'t pin widgets automatically — long-press the home screen → Widgets → Seconds Clock
